name: Daily Mail cryptic crossword, book 2 No 81

book.title: Daily Mail New Cryptic Crosswords, volume 2

clue.text: Not afraid to capture one soldier without finally going away

indicators.note: capturing something means holding it inside, so the bold word wraps round the rest
without its final letter means the soldier word loses its last letter

blocks.note: bold, unafraid
the Roman numeral for one
a sapper is a military engineer

explanation.surface: A soldier, no coward, seizes another while slipping off.
explanation.walkthrough: The soldier is a sapper, a military engineer; 'without finally' trims it before it goes, with the Roman one, inside the word for bold.
explanation.definitionFit: Something disappearing is vanishing from view, leaving or departing.

clue.text: Cover up girl in a predicament

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: a lid covers a pot
a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl must hide something and finds herself in trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: A dilemma is an awkward situation offering only unwelcome choices, a fix or quandary.

clue.text: Gripped for a time and tied up

blocks.note: a spell is a period of time
bound means fastened with rope

explanation.surface: Someone held captive for a while, tied and restrained.
explanation.definitionFit: Spellbound describes an audience held fascinated and enthralled, unable to look away.

clue.text: A spinner turning up with low parts one can eat

definitions.note: a phrase meaning things that are eaten, standing for a plural noun

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means the words are read from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: taken as written
a spinning top is a toy that spins
the body parts at the bottom of the feet

explanation.surface: A cricket spinner bowling with toes on view, all oddly edible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spinner' suggests a cricket bowler, but here it is the child's spinning toy; 'A' is reversed along with it.
explanation.definitionFit: Potatoes are starchy tubers, a staple vegetable that people eat boiled, mashed or fried.

clue.text: Use some of them on manoeuvre

blocks.note: 'em is the clipped spoken form of the pronoun
a ploy is a tactical move

explanation.surface: Deploy a few of the troops during military exercises.
explanation.definitionFit: To employ something is to make use of it or put it to work.

clue.text: Complain about the train service

blocks.note: first meaning: to protest bitterly against
second meaning: the railway as a means of travel

explanation.surface: A commuter grumbling about late trains.
explanation.walkthrough: To rail against something is to complain loudly; going by rail is going by train.
explanation.definitionFit: Rail is both a verb for protesting angrily and a noun for railway transport.

clue.text: Complete opposition to everything

blocks.note: surface reading: a protester against every single thing
setter's reading: the exact opposite of everything, which is zero, not a thing at all

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a description of a contrarian, but the opposite of everything is simply its absence.
explanation.definitionFit: Nothing is the absence of anything at all, the logical reverse of everything.

clue.text: Fools have to go in for each that appears adequate

indicators.note: going in means being placed inside the next piece

blocks.note: an ass is a fool
must means have to
per means for each, as in per head

explanation.surface: Idiots must enter one by one for something that seems good enough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fools' looks like the subject of the sentence; it is just the first of two pieces wrapped inside the Latin-derived word for each.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass muster is to be judged acceptable, meeting the required standard on inspection.

clue.text: Complaint of one in mental difficulty

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another
letters in difficulty are troubled and thrown out of order

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for one
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone suffering mental trouble is moaning about it.
explanation.definitionFit: A complaint in the medical sense is an illness or disorder, a minor ailment.

clue.text: One has the art needed for tying up a boat

definitions.text: needed for tying up a boat

blocks.note: first meaning: an artist who works in paint

blocks.clueFragment: needed for tying up a boat
blocks.note: second meaning: a rope at the bow used to moor a small boat

explanation.surface: Someone skilled at knotting mooring ropes.
explanation.walkthrough: A painter is also a nautical term for the line attached to the bow of a dinghy.
explanation.definitionFit: An artist working in oils is a painter, and so is the mooring line on a small craft.

clue.text: Food and drink for new students when rest is disturbed all round

indicators.note: disturbed letters are shaken out of their order
all round means these letters surround the other piece

blocks.note: taken as written
freshmen are first-year students

explanation.surface: Snacks laid on for first-years whose sleep has been interrupted.
explanation.walkthrough: Freshmen is the usual word for first-year university students, especially in America.
explanation.definitionFit: Refreshments are light snacks and drinks served at an event or break.

clue.text: Mimicry allows no time for excitement

indicators.note: allowing no letter means that letter is removed

blocks.note: T is the abbreviation for time
stimulation is arousal or excitement

explanation.surface: Imitating others leaves no time for thrills.
explanation.definitionFit: A simulation is an imitation or pretence, copying the appearance of something real.

clue.text: One goes to law without obvious disagreement

indicators.note: without means the following piece is taken away

blocks.note: a plaintiff brings a lawsuit
plain means clear, obvious

explanation.surface: Someone sues though the quarrel is not obvious.
explanation.walkthrough: PLAINTIFF minus PLAIN leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiff is a petty quarrel, a minor squabble between friends or partners.

clue.text: Noble rider's new look has the edge

indicators.note: giving the letters a new look means rearranging them

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An aristocratic horseman's fresh style gives him an advantage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has the edge' suggests winning, but 'has' joins and 'the edge' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A borderline is a boundary, the line marking where one area ends.

clue.text: Given time to become mature

blocks.note: first meaning: left to dry and age, like timber or wine
second meaning: experienced, a veteran

explanation.surface: Something left to age until ready.
explanation.walkthrough: Seasoned wood has been left for a season; a seasoned player is experienced.
explanation.definitionFit: Seasoned means aged until ready, and of people, experienced and practised.

clue.text: Achieve understanding in depth

blocks.note: first meaning: slang for get or appreciate something
second meaning: to excavate, going down into the ground

explanation.walkthrough: 'I dig it' is slang for 'I understand it'.
explanation.definitionFit: Dig is informal for grasp or like, and literally means excavate soil downward.

clue.text: People don’t live here in hired room or guest house

indicators.note: in means the letters lie inside the run of words that follows

blocks.note: spanning the end of one word, a whole word and the start of another

explanation.surface: A lodging house where no one stays permanently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'People don't live here' reads like a rented room, but it means the bodies are dead.
explanation.definitionFit: A mortuary holds corpses, so nobody there is alive.

clue.text: Mistake getting left out to take a drink

indicators.note: out means the letter for left is dropped

blocks.note: a slip is an error
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: An error made after being excluded drives someone to drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking liquid in tiny mouthfuls, a little at a time, is the plain verb sense here.

clue.text: Those who intrude to steal and cook eggs?

blocks.note: first meaning: trespassers who hunt game illegally
second meaning: pans used to cook eggs gently in water

explanation.surface: Burglars who break in and then make breakfast.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the second sense: an egg poacher is a kitchen pan, so poachers cook eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: Poachers illegally take game from another's land; poachers are also pans for cooking eggs.

clue.text: Go straight into relaxation, it seems

definitions.note: a phrase for going into a relaxed state, standing for a verb

blocks.note: first meaning: to straighten out from a bent shape
second meaning: to drop one's stiffness and become less formal

explanation.walkthrough: 'Go straight' hints at a reformed criminal, but it means literally becoming straight, as a bent rod does.
explanation.definitionFit: To unbend is to straighten something out, and figuratively to relax and loosen up.

clue.text: Go from pub to pub to find a girl

blocks.note: a bar is a pub, taken twice
taken as written

explanation.surface: A pub crawl in search of a girlfriend.
explanation.definitionFit: Barbara is a woman's given name, a girl in crossword terms.

clue.text: What's valuable if turned to quieten swimmer

indicators.note: turned means the short word is read backwards

blocks.note: gold is precious
taken as written
sh is the call for quiet

explanation.surface: Silencing a swimmer who turned out to be worth something.
explanation.definitionFit: A goldfish is an orange pet fish that swims in a bowl.

clue.text: Pictures one has in mind of one bad game on line

indicators.note: a bad version is a corrupted one, so the letters are muddled

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for one
taken as written
RY is short for railway, a rail line

explanation.surface: A loser imagines a poorly played match over the phone.
explanation.walkthrough: RY, railway, is a standard crossword abbreviation for line.
explanation.definitionFit: Imagery is mental pictures, visual images formed in the imagination.

clue.text: Words that don't start are the last to go on in time

indicators.note: not starting means losing the first letter

blocks.note: a text is written words
the end is the last part

explanation.surface: A speech whose opening is cut runs on past its finish.
explanation.definitionFit: To extend is to prolong or lengthen in duration, to last longer.

clue.text: Racing for a patch of influence

blocks.note: first meaning: horse racing as a sport
second meaning: home territory controlled by someone

explanation.surface: A gang fighting for control of an area.
explanation.walkthrough: The turf is a traditional British name for horse racing.
explanation.definitionFit: Turf means horse racing generally, and also one's own territory or sphere of control.

clue.text: Tax beer perhaps with one put in to make it worse

indicators.note: perhaps hints the letters are only one possible arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written
an ace is a one in cards

explanation.surface: A duty on beer is a cost that only aggravates matters.
explanation.definitionFit: To exacerbate a problem is to aggravate or intensify it.

clue.text: Tree it's glorious to be under

blocks.note: sublime means glorious
sub- means under

explanation.surface: Sitting under a tree is wonderful.
explanation.walkthrough: Put SUB under the tree and you have SUBLIME, so SUBLIME without SUB is the tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The lime, or linden, is a broad-leaved tree.

clue.text: See rail crash and get to understand

indicators.note: a crash smashes things up, so the letters are scattered

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Witnessing a train accident and grasping what happened.
explanation.definitionFit: To realise is to become aware of something, grasping it fully.

clue.text: I have returned to make an impression as you can see

indicators.note: returned means going back, so the short form runs backwards

blocks.note: I've is the contracted form
a dent is a hollow impression

explanation.surface: Coming back to leave a mark that everyone notices.
explanation.definitionFit: Evident means plain to see, clear and obvious.

clue.text: Harry had bees fluttering in the shop

indicators.note: fluttering things flit about, so the letters move around

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Bees buzzing around a man in a store.
explanation.definitionFit: A haberdashery is a shop selling sewing goods, or in America menswear.
